blurb:
Marietta Melt Yard is one of those spots you end up at when the whole crew is together and nobody wants to overthink it. We took the family here on a weekend and the vibe is easy, casual, and loud in a good way. Good for a weekday lunch or a Friday dinner when you want something satisfying without a lot of fuss.

The menu is grilled and melty comfort food, and people keep coming back for it. A couple folks in our group felt their food ran a little on the greasy side, so just know going in that this is not a light meal. If that's your thing on a given night, you'll be happy.

One genuinely funny thing: the napkins are so thick and heavy that my wife grabbed one and thought it was a cloth napkin. Turns out it's paper. Small detail, but it says something about the place that they even thought about that.

blurb:
If you want wings, cold beer, and somewhere with actual energy, The Wing Cafe on Roswell Road delivers. This is a post-game spot, a Friday night spot, or just a we-need-somewhere-fun spot. The outdoor tiki bar is a good time and they do live music, so the vibe on weekends can get going in the best way.

The wings are the whole point here and they have a solid craft beer selection to back them up. It's loud, it's casual, and nobody's going home hungry. Good for groups, good for sports, good for pretty much any night you don't want to sit somewhere quiet.

They're open until 11pm every night of the week, which is genuinely useful in a neighborhood where a lot of spots shut down early.

blurb:
Derek's is our Saturday morning spot. It's a breakfast and lunch place on Canton Road that's been doing it right for a long time. Friendly servers, no attitude, no wait that makes you question whether it's worth it. It always is.

The French toast is what I get almost every time, usually with a couple eggs and bacon on the side. Simple and done well, which is really all you want at 8am. It's a great place to bring kids and it's laid back enough that nobody's stressed out about the little ones making noise.

They're closed Sundays and they wrap up at 2:30pm every day, so this is strictly a morning and early afternoon operation. Get there, get a table, and take your time.

blurb:
JJ's is the neighborhood pizza spot people kick themselves for not finding sooner. It's in a strip mall on Roswell Road and it's very easy to overlook, which is a shame because the pizza is genuinely good. My wife and I have made it our go-to for a low-key Friday night in.

Order the garlic cheese knots. That's not optional. The stuffed pizza has a fan base for good reason too. It's not what you expect if you've never had a stuffed-style pie, but once you try it you'll get it immediately.

Just know they're closed on Tuesdays, so plan accordingly. It's a small place and it earns every one of those 4.5 stars.

blurb:
This place is a hidden gem and I mean that seriously. It's tucked inside a supermarket on Allgood Road and if you drive past it without knowing, you'd never stop. But the people who know, know.

The al pastor is the move. It's well seasoned, cooked right, and the tortas they stuff it into are legit. The pupusas are worth ordering too, specifically the beans and cheese. The chicken plate with rice and homemade beans has a following for good reason. You can tell the chicken is marinated overnight because it actually has flavor, not just char.

Prices are low and portions are real. This is a great lunch stop or an easy weeknight dinner if you're in the area and want something honest and good.
